title: Tier A: a green card on approval
status: decided, memo 1 A, parts 1 and 3; tier A's cutoff DEC-2026-11-12-12
parameters: Four groups, each present in the United States on January 1 of the year the act is enacted (tier A's cutoff, IMM-1.04, `DEC-2026-11-12-12`): (1) people who arrived before 18, with a schooling, work or service test (the Dream Act's); (2) anyone who has held TPS, DACA or humanitarian parole at any time; (3) workers with at least 1,035 hours or 180 days of farm, care or construction work in the two years before applying, on the farmworker bill's test [EV-IMM-522], extended to care and construction (care's first ask, `DEC-2026-11-11-04` point 8; housing's workforce condition); (4) their spouses and minor children present on that date. Work history is shown as residence is (IMM-1.06): records first (W-2s, posted earnings, H-2A and employer records), then a sworn statement plus one document per gap, where a statement by an employer, co-worker, union or care recipient counts as the document (working choice, after the farmworker bill's evidence rule). Permanent residence on approval; citizenship after three years (IMM-1.14)

title: Tier B: ten years' residence, counted to the day a person applies
parameters: Ten years' continuous residence before the day of application, through the registry's rolling date (IMM-1.05), with a clean record (IMM-1.08). Permanent residence on approval; citizenship on the five-year clock. A person with eight years in 2029 qualifies in 2031. Brief absences do not break residence (working choice: up to 180 days in one trip, 365 in all over ten years, as the U.S. Citizenship Act counts them)

title: Registered status for everyone else present on the day the act is signed
parameters: A person present on the day the act is signed (registration's cutoff, IMM-1.04) who is not in tier A or B registers once, gives biometrics and passes IMM-1.08's check. They receive registered status: a work permit and protection from removal, valid until the person reaches ten years' residence and the registry (IMM-1.05), with no renewal filing. USCIS keeps the record current from its own, the IRS's and SSA's records, and the status ends only for a bar those records show, after notice (working choice). Time in registered status counts toward tier B's ten years, and the green card comes at ten years. Registered status is not a bar to any other route

title: Two cutoffs: tier A on January 1 of the year of enactment; registration on the day the act is signed
status: decided, point 1 as Espen answered it, `DEC-2026-11-12-12`
parameters: *Tier A* (IMM-1.01): presence on January 1 of the calendar year in which the act is enacted. *Registered status* (IMM-1.03): presence on the day the President signs the act. *Tier B* (IMM-1.02, 1.05) has no cutoff: it is the rolling ten years. Proof follows IMM-1.06: the records that show a person here before the date. *What the two dates do:* a person who arrives during the year of enactment, before signature, registers rather than entering tier A, and reaches a green card through the registry at ten years. The debate year cannot draw people into the green-card-on-approval tier, and no date after the law is known opens any route. Filing opens separately, no later than 270 days after signature (IMM-1.05). Cost: the earlier tier A date moves about 50,000 people (range 20,000-100,000; working assumption) from tier A to registered status, lowering memo 1's line by about $0.3 billion over FY2030-39 (`tools/immigration_model.py`, `tier_a_late_arrivals_m`)

title: The registry, 8 U.S.C. 1259, with a rolling date of ten years before the day of application
parameters: 1259's fixed January 1, 1972 is replaced by "the date ten years before the date of the application". 1259's existing conditions stay: continuous residence, good moral character, and not inadmissible as a criminal, subversive, narcotics violator or smuggler (narrowed by IMM-1.08). It carries tier B and is the route for registered people at ten years. No closing window. Filing for the registry, tier A and registration opens on one form no later than 270 days after the act's signature (working choice; about October 1, 2030 on the working timeline)

title: Records first: proof of residence from what the government holds
parameters: USCIS checks the years against records the government holds: tax returns filed with an individual taxpayer number or any Social Security number, earnings posted at SSA, school enrollment, court and DHS files, and other federal records the act lists. Where records run out, a sworn statement plus any one document per gap year covers it. False statements carry the existing fraud penalties. A published fraud audit each year, with a review trigger (IMM-6.06). No document hunt beyond the gaps

title: People USCIS already knows start on a notice
parameters: DACA, TPS and parole holders, past or present, whose biometrics and files USCIS holds, receive a notice of what the records show: their tier A eligibility and years of residence. They confirm or correct it, and are approved on the notice unless the check (IMM-1.08) finds a bar. Notices go out first, in the opening months

title: Vetting and bars
parameters: Biometrics and a criminal and security check for everyone. The bars are 1259's existing grounds [EV-IMM-623], with no bar for immigration-only offenses (unlawful entry and reentry, 8 U.S.C. 1325 and 1326, and status violations), and a waiver for convictions more than ten years old or minor (working choice: no prison term over one year), granted for family unity, humanitarian reasons or the public interest. *The immigration-only grounds, for every route (tier A, tier B through the registry, registration):* 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), (a)(5), (a)(7) and (a)(9)(B) do not apply [EV-IMM-649] [EV-IMM-651]; (a)(6)(A), (a)(6)(C) and (a)(9)(C) do not apply unless they rest on an unlawful entry after the act's signature [EV-IMM-647] [EV-IMM-648] [EV-IMM-652]; (a)(6)(B) and (a)(9)(A) do not apply unless the conduct began after filing [EV-IMM-650]. That is S. 744's list [EV-IMM-654]. Any other ground except the criminal, security and terrorism grounds 1259 keeps may be waived for family unity, humanitarian reasons or the public interest. *Old orders:* the reinstatement bar of 8 U.S.C. 1231(a)(5) [EV-IMM-653] does not apply to any route; a person with a final order of removal, deportation or exclusion may file notwithstanding it, and the order is vacated on approval without a motion (working choice; S. 744 required a motion to reopen [EV-IMM-656]). 1.6 million people on the non-detained docket had a final order in February 2026 [EV-IMM-170]
agency: DHS (USCIS), with the FBI; DOJ (EOIR) for old orders

title: No penalty; no fee below 200% of poverty; a capped fee above
parameters: No penalty for any route. No fee for a person whose household income is below 200% of the poverty guideline, shown by the same records (IMM-1.06) or attestation. Above that, a fee at cost, capped per family (working choice: the cap is the fee for two adults), payable in instalments. The waiver is claimed on the form, with no separate request

title: Protection from the day the act is signed; a work permit from the day of filing
parameters: DHS (USCIS); DOJ (EOIR)

title: Back taxes only as the IRS assesses them
parameters: No reconstruction of past income by the applicant. Taxes already assessed on income already earned are paid or put on an IRS instalment plan, which does not delay approval

title: Work-eligible Social Security numbers from registration
parameters: Each person granted registered status, tier A or tier B receives a work-eligible Social Security number, issued by SSA from USCIS's record without a separate visit. Earnings already posted under another number are credited to the person's own record on their request. Legalized parents then meet the 2025 child credit's number rule [EV-IMM-050], and earnings post to their own records

title: Temporary statuses lead to permanence
parameters: Time in TPS, deferred action, parole or registered status counts toward tier B's ten years. TPS stays as an emergency tool. DACA work permits, which the Fifth Circuit found severable [EV-IMM-027], continue until each holder is approved

title: The clock to citizenship
parameters: Tier A: naturalization three years after the green card. Tier B and registered people who reach ten years: the ordinary five-year clock. Naturalization's fee rule is IMM-5.04

title: A route from abroad for long-settled residents removed or pushed out in 2025-28, for family unity
status: decided (Espen, November 12, lead session; milestone review question 1)
parameters: A person removed, or who departed, on or after January 20, 2025 and before the act is signed (2025-28 as decided, carried to signature so no gap opens before IMM-1.10's protection; working choice), who had at least three years' continuous presence before leaving, and who is the spouse, parent or child of a citizen, a permanent resident or a person granted status under the act, may apply from abroad for the route they would have met but for leaving: tier A, tier B or registration, with registration's protection given on parole for the purpose. The presence requirement is waived, and so are the bars for prior removal and reentry (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(A) and (C)) and reinstatement (1231(a)(5)). Filing is online or at a consulate, with the interview abroad; State and DHS set the procedure. The model is the U.S. Citizenship Act of 2021 [EV-IMM-658], with S. 744's family-unity waiver for people who had reentered [EV-IMM-657]. ICE reported 442,640 removals in FY2025 and 483,200 in FY2026 [EV-IMM-659]; how many meet the test is not known. Cost (working assumption): about 50,000 returnees (range 20,000-150,000), about $6.6 billion over FY2030-39 for their coverage and cases (section 6, part 1)
cost_source: 6-cost.md, part 1 (memo 6's line: the returnees' coverage and their cases from abroad, about $6.6 billion over FY2030-39)

title: One eligibility title
parameters: One title amends each program's eligibility section. It adds memo 1's statuses (tier A and B permanent residents, registered status) to the 1996 law's "qualified alien" list (8 U.S.C. 1641) and to Section 214's list (42 U.S.C. 1436a). It reverses the 2025 law's limits [EV-IMM-046] to [EV-IMM-050] as each row below says. A program not listed follows the law before July 2025

title: The single health plan: everyone with lawful or registered status, from wave 1; emergency care for people with no status
status: decided, memo 6 C as amended for health (Espen, November 12, lead session)
parameters: From the first wave on January 1, 2031, the single plan covers residents who are citizens or hold any lawful or registered status: permanent residents, registered status (IMM-1.03), a pending filing under the act (its receipt, IMM-1.10; counting it is a working choice), asylum applicants, parolees, TPS holders and lawful temporary workers, including H-2A and H-2B workers and the portable farm, care and construction visas (IMM-2.08 to 2.10). People with no status receive emergency care as today: hospitals' duty to screen and stabilize (EMTALA) and Emergency Medicaid, which stay at their January 2029 terms. *How status is checked:* enrollment asks CMS to confirm status from USCIS's own records (IMM-6.06's match), with no new document from the person; a person USCIS has no record for may attest and give one document, as IMM-1.06 allows. The data firewall (IMM-1.36) bars any enforcement use of the check. This answers care's point 3 and amends `DEC-2026-11-12-07`'s memo 6 C for health coverage only; the rest of the table stands. Espen: "they will either (a) be registered with the universal healthcare system, in which case they will need to be documented immigrants or, (b) they will receive emergency care that would typically fall into the current-day uncompensated bucket"

title: Medicaid and premium credits before the waves
parameters: The pre-2025 law is restored (HLT-1.02, care's, decided and priced there). Memo 1's new permanent residents qualify with no five-year wait. People without status keep emergency Medicaid and state options

title: The long-term care benefit (2035): every resident
parameters: As the single plan: residence, no status question (`DEC-2026-11-11-02`)

title: Child care and pre-K: every resident child
parameters: No status question (`DEC-2026-11-11-03`). Head Start follows its rules before July 2025

title: The child benefit: the child's own ID, no parent rule
parameters: Cited here as the table's row; specified as the secure floor's FAM-1.04: a child qualifies with their own Social Security number, adoption number or individual taxpayer number

title: The earned income credit
parameters: As now: a work-eligible Social Security number. Memo 1's statuses carry one from registration (IMM-1.12)

title: SNAP, SSI and TANF: the pre-2025 law, with no five-year wait for memo 1's new permanent residents
parameters: SNAP's immigrant rule (2025 law, sec. 10108) returns to the pre-2025 law. That restoration is priced by the secure floor's SNAP repeal (INC-2.01), not counted again here. SSI and TANF follow the pre-2025 law. Memo 1's new permanent residents qualify with no five-year wait: their years of residence count as the wait. Registered status is a qualified status, with the five-year wait for adults counted from the day of registration (working choice, consistent with memo 6's pricing; most registered people reach ten years and a green card first)

title: Medicare
parameters: The 2025 limit [EV-IMM-048] is reversed: lawfully present people qualify as before 2025; memo 1's statuses as permanent residents. People without status: no (contributory rules)

title: Social Security and paid leave
parameters: By earnings with a work-eligible number, as now (IMM-1.12)

title: Rental help: Section 214 with registered status added; proration kept
parameters: Mixed-status families are prorated (`DEC-2026-11-09-10`); one member is verified, the rest are not required to be

title: The owner and buyer programs: the owner of record
parameters: A mixed-status family qualifies for HOU-10 to HOU-12 through the owner of record, checked through records the agency can query, as rental help qualifies through proration. Answers housing's open item

title: FHA and USDA loans: FHA's 2025 rule for non-permanent residents reversed
parameters: Lawfully present non-permanent residents, registered status included, qualify for FHA and USDA guaranteed loans as before the 2025 rule

title: The property-tax match (HOU-11): not a federal public benefit
parameters: Written outside 8 U.S.C. 1611 and 1621: relief follows the tax bill, with no status question

title: Farmworker housing (USDA 514/516): as rental help
status: proposed to housing, memo 6 C; `DEC-2026-11-10-02` item 5
parameters: Prorated in a mixed family, as Section 214 does

title: The emergency rent fund (HOU-1D): no status test
parameters: Short-term emergency aid on self-attestation; the landlord is checked, not the tenant

title: One data firewall
parameters: What a person gives any plan program or the registry (IMM-1.05 to 1.07), and what the plan's shared records hold, may not be used or shared for immigration enforcement, except under a criminal warrant for a named person. Each use is logged; misuse carries civil and criminal penalties and a private right of action. It matches housing's rule (`DEC-2026-11-09-11`) and care's (HLT-7.21). IMM-4.11 writes the enforcement side

title: Recapture of unused numbers
parameters: Family and employment numbers unused in any year since FY1992 go back into the pool, used over five years from FY2031 (working choice). Unused numbers roll forward automatically from then on

title: Spouses and minor children of permanent residents outside the caps
parameters: Treated as immediate relatives, as citizens' are

title: The employment per-country cap lifted over three years
parameters: 7% [EV-IMM-121] to 15% in FY2031, 25% in FY2032, none from FY2033 (working phase). The family per-country cap rises to 15%

title: The 2024 bill's higher numbers, made permanent
parameters: The family-sponsored level from 480,000 to 512,000 and its floor from 226,000 to 258,000; the employment level from 140,000 to 158,000, each year from FY2031 [EV-IMM-535]

title: Protection for children who age out
parameters: A child's age is fixed on the day the petition is filed. Children who were lawfully present as dependents of long-term visa holders keep their place, on the America's CHILDREN Act model [EV-IMM-518]

title: H-1B selection ranked by offered wage
status: decided, memo 3 part 1 A, in B
parameters: Petitions are ranked by the offered wage's level against the local wage for the occupation, highest first, replacing the lottery

title: A statutory H-1B fee, retained by USCIS and a training fund
status: decided, memo 3 part 1 A, in B; R1
parameters: About $5,000 to $10,000 a petition by employer size (legacy estimate), indexed, retained by USCIS and an apprenticeship and training fund (ledger IF1, about $0.015 trillion over FY2030-39). It replaces the proclamation charge, which runs to September 2027 [EV-IMM-056] [EV-IMM-057]

title: Farm: the Farm Workforce Modernization Act's route
parameters: Certified agricultural worker status for current farmworkers on the bill's hours test, and its H-2A reform [EV-IMM-522] [EV-IMM-523]. Memo 1's tier A gives current farmworkers a green card on approval, so the bill's certified status serves farmworkers present on the day the act is signed (registration's cutoff) who arrived after January 1 of the year of enactment (tier A's cutoff, IMM-1.04), on the bill's hours test. A farmworker who arrives after signature comes through the H-2A reform, not certified status, so no route opens after the law is known

title: A portable care-worker visa
parameters: For direct care occupations: paid at least the care wage floor (`DEC-2026-11-11-04`, memo 14: $20 an hour in 2026 dollars, indexed); portable between care employers without a new petition; a green card after three years of care work. Spouses and children come with the worker. Care occupations count on any shortage list (care's third ask)

title: A portable construction-worker visa
parameters: For construction trades: paid at least the local prevailing wage; portable between construction employers; a green card after three years; tied to the decided building programs (housing's production and repair, transportation's construction)

title: Numbers for the care and construction routes set each year from the decided programs' hiring needs
status: decided, memo 3 part 2 B; ceiling a working choice
parameters: The Labor Department publishes, each year, the hiring needs of the decided programs (care's guarantees, housing's and transportation's construction) and sets each route's number, up to a statutory ceiling (working choice: 50,000 a year for each route at the start, reviewed after three years). A review trigger pauses new visas in a route whose national unemployment rate is above its five-year average by two points or more

title: Employer attestation, not a tie to one employer
parameters: The employer attests to the wage and the job. The worker carries no tie to one employer and may change jobs within the route on notice. Wage and Hour enforces the attestation (IMM-4.16). The wage and portability rules go to the work flagship (shared rule 8)

title: Asylum officers decide first, within 180 days
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 D; the act
parameters: The 2022 rule's officer merits process in statute [EV-IMM-300] [EV-IMM-301], extended to affirmative claims. A decision within 180 days of filing. A denial goes to the immigration court for review on the record, with new evidence allowed; a grant is final unless DHS appeals on the law

title: A surge rule that adds capacity, not a bar
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 D; the act
parameters: When southwest border encounters average 5,000 a day over seven consecutive days (the 2024 bill's number [EV-IMM-533]; working choice), the Secretary must, within 14 days: detail asylum officers and judges to reception centers near the border; decide claims there in a 90-day track on the EU's model [EV-IMM-458]; and release people to case management (IMM-4.06) or hold them only under IMM-4.03's priorities and IMM-4.05's cap. Asylum at and between ports stays available. The rule ends when the average falls below 3,500 for 14 days (working choice). Each activation is reported to Congress with its decisions and times

title: Access to claims from the region
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 D; R1 money
parameters: Refugee and parole processing abroad, defined as access to a claim, never detention abroad [EV-IMM-462]

title: A refugee floor of 50,000 admissions a year, funded
parameters: At least 50,000 admissions a year in statute, binding admissions and not only the ceiling [EV-IMM-465], with the money in R1; private sponsorship above the floor on Canada's model [EV-IMM-466]. The President sets the ceiling above the floor. The floor sits below every ceiling from FY1981 to FY2016 [EV-IMM-634] [EV-IMM-463]

title: The 2025-26 measures ended
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 D; executive, January 20, 2029
parameters: Proclamation 10888's use against asylum seekers ends [EV-IMM-053]; the 2026 no-interview referral rule is withdrawn [EV-IMM-305]; the FY2029 refugee ceiling is set at or above 50,000

title: The asylum charges that grow with delay repealed
parameters: Repeal the $100-a-year asylum-pending fee and the $550 first work permit charge for asylum applicants [EV-IMM-043] [EV-IMM-045]. An asylum applicant's work permit after 150 days, without the new charge

title: Unobligated wall money redirected to evidence-backed border security
parameters: The balance of the 2025 law's $46.55 billion border wall appropriation unobligated on the day R1 is enacted [EV-IMM-034] is made available until September 30, 2034 for: screening technology at ports of entry; Border Patrol processing and staffing; surveillance and detection technology; search and rescue; and barrier construction, repair or maintenance at locations where the Border Patrol's published operational requirements recommend it. Each wall project needs a published needs assessment by the Chief of the Border Patrol, consultation with the affected tribes, landowners and local governments, and the environmental review the 2025 law would otherwise waive. CBP reports each year what the money bought

title: Court capacity: the 800-judge cap repealed, and the corps sized to clear the backlog in about six years
status: decided, memo 4 part 2; proposed to CRT-5
parameters: Repeal the cap from November 1, 2028 [EV-IMM-105]. Judges with their teams (clerks, staff attorneys, interpreters, space) sized to clear the backlog by FY2035 at the inflow after legalization. *Working assumption* (`tools/immigration_model.py`, `eoir()`): about 1,670 judges in all, about 920 more than the 753 on board [EV-IMM-103] (range about 860-2,400 in all; at the slow end of completions a judge even 250 hires a year clear the backlog only by FY2036), hired about 250 a year from FY2030 so the corps peaks by FY2033, and shrinking by attrition (about 5.6% a year [EV-IMM-646]) once the backlog clears in FY2035. It rests on CRS's average of about 510 completions a judge [EV-IMM-641] (range 450-750), not the higher recent rates that in absentia orders inflate [EV-IMM-106]. CRS found 700 more judges than its 649 would clear a smaller backlog by FY2032 [EV-IMM-642]; the Manhattan Institute, about 250 more a year at 957 completions a judge [EV-IMM-646]. *Cost:* about $1.5 million a judge team a year [EV-IMM-644] [EV-IMM-645], about $13 billion over FY2030-39 (section 6). *A slower ramp:* at 150 hires a year, EOIR's FY2024 request [EV-IMM-644], the same corps clears the backlog about FY2037, two years late; at 800 judges it does not clear within fifteen years. The number is set with democratic renewal, whose CRT-5 carries the court

title: Timelines
status: decided, memo 4 part 2; proposed to CRT-5
parameters: Detained cases decided within 90 days; review of an officer's asylum denial within 180 days; non-detained cases within two years once the backlog is cleared

title: Notice and limits on orders in absentia
status: decided, memo 4 part 2; proposed to CRT-5
parameters: Hearing notices go to the address in the records the government holds (IMM-1.06), with a right to reopen an order issued without proper notice; 15% of in absentia orders in 2008-18 were later overturned [EV-IMM-316]

title: Independence
status: decided, memo 4 part 2; proposed to CRT-5
parameters: Judges not removable at will by the Attorney General; the 2026 court bill's Article I structure [EV-IMM-113] is the base CRT-5 uses. Its form, tenure and fallback stay with democratic renewal

title: Appointed counsel for children, people with serious mental illness and everyone detained
parameters: Government-appointed counsel in removal proceedings for children, people found to have a serious mental illness, and every detained person. Children's counsel runs through HHS's refugee office; the others through a DOJ program until CRT-5 exists. The 2026 court bill appoints none [EV-IMM-114]

title: ICE replaced; DHS's immigration functions restructured
parameters: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is abolished on the transition date (working choice: October 1, 2031, about 21 months after signature, once registration is open). DHS's immigration work is organized in four lines, each led by a Senate-confirmed head: (1) *border and ports*, CBP, unchanged in mission; (2) *benefits and humanitarian processing*, USCIS, with the asylum officer corps and the surge rule's reception centers (IMM-3.01, 3.02); (3) *interior immigration enforcement*, a new component that takes over removal operations under IMM-4.03 to 4.10, with its case-management service run separately from arrests (IMM-4.06); (4) *criminal investigations* (IMM-4.02). The act names the new components; this dossier commits to no name ("Humanitarian Processing Service" is not adopted). Personnel, contracts and appropriations transfer by function. Officers are re-credentialed under the new rules, with training in them before the transition date

title: Criminal investigations a separate component
parameters: Homeland Security Investigations' work on smuggling, trafficking, child exploitation, customs fraud and transnational crime becomes its own DHS component. It makes no civil immigration arrests except of a person who is the subject of its criminal case. The Secure America Act's $7.45 billion for it lapses with the rest in 2029 [EV-IMM-040]; FY2030 appropriations carry it

title: Enforcement priorities in statute
parameters: National security, public safety (a conviction for a serious crime, as the act lists) and recent unlawful entry (after the day the act is signed, registration's cutoff, IMM-1.04, and within the last two years, working choice) come first. Each arrest outside them carries a written reason, reviewed by a supervisor and counted in a published monthly report. The rules bind every officer exercising immigration authority, including state and local partners (IMM-4.10)

title: Enforceable detention standards
parameters: Standards for medical care, conditions, access to counsel and family contact set by rule and binding on every facility, contract and local jail used. People held may sue to enforce them; a facility failing two inspections in a row loses its contract. Every death in custody is reviewed and published within 90 days

title: A cap of 30,000 on average daily detention
status: decided, memo 5, A's rules; funded in FY2030 appropriations
parameters: Average daily detention over a fiscal year may not exceed 30,000 [EV-IMM-571]. An emergency waiver for up to 90 days, renewable once, when the surge rule is active (IMM-3.02) and priority cases exceed the cap, reported to Congress within 7 days with its reasons. A sustained rise in priority arrests above the cap for two years is answered by statute, not by waiver (memo 5). FY2030 appropriations fund the cap from October 1, 2029, when the reconciliation money lapses [EV-IMM-035]

title: Case management as the default
parameters: People outside the priorities are released to case management, not held: a case manager, help with legal counsel, housing and schooling, and reminders of hearings, on the Family Case Management Program's model [EV-IMM-355] [EV-IMM-357]. It is run by nonprofit and local providers under contract, separate from the arrest function. Electronic monitoring only where a judge or a written risk finding requires it. Appearance rates are published

title: Protected places
parameters: No arrest, search or surveillance at or near schools, places of worship, hospitals and clinics, courthouses, shelters and disaster sites without a judicial warrant or exigent circumstances, which are recorded and reported

title: Officer identification: one statute with the executive-power file
parameters: Visible name or badge number and agency on every officer making an arrest; no face coverings except in documented undercover work. One statute for every federal law-enforcement officer, referenced from both files (staging 5.11)

title: An independent detention inspector
status: working choice, to make IMM-4.04 enforceable
parameters: A detention inspector inside DHS's Office of Inspector General, with unannounced inspections of every facility at least once a year, public reports and the power to recommend ending a contract

title: Delegated authority only on the same rules
parameters: Agreements that let state and local police exercise immigration authority (section 287(g); 2,506 signed by September 2026 [EV-IMM-180]) continue only if the partner is bound by IMM-4.03 to 4.08. Existing agreements end on the transition date (IMM-4.01) unless renewed on those terms

title: The firewall's enforcement side
parameters: No immigration enforcement component may request, receive or use data barred by IMM-1.36, including registry and registration files, the plan's program records and the labor agencies' complaint files (IMM-4.17). Breach is a violation subject to IMM-1.36's penalties

title: E-Verify permanent and mandatory, phased in by employer size
parameters: The pilot's sunset is struck, as the 2026 Mandatory E-Verify Act would [EV-IMM-633]; E-Verify's authority has lapsed and been extended in appropriations [EV-IMM-397]. Every employer checks each new hire, within three working days of the start of work, in four tranches a year apart: (1) employers with 500 or more employees; (2) 100-499; (3) 20-99; (4) 1-19, household employers and agricultural employers. No tranche starts before the date IMM-4.13 sets. Existing employees are not re-checked (working choice: the burden of re-checking falls on long-settled workers and buys little once they hold status). Federal contractors' current duty continues

title: The mandate's start: no earlier than October 1 of the year after enactment, and only on a passing check
parameters: *The earliest date:* the first tranche (IMM-4.12) starts no earlier than October 1 of the calendar year after the year of enactment (October 1, 2030 on the working timeline). *The check:* on that date the DHS Inspector General confirms whether all of these hold: (a) filing for the registry, tier A and registration (IMM-1.05) is open nationwide, online, on paper and at every front door (IMM-6.04); (b) everyone USCIS already knows (DACA, TPS and parole holders in its files) has received their notice (IMM-1.07); (c) work permits are issued and E-Verify queries run within the act's statutory time limits: the filing receipt within 14 days and recorded in E-Verify's and SSA's records within 30 days of filing (IMM-1.10), and contests answered within ten federal working days (IMM-4.14); (d) the systems that do (c) exist and are in use; (e) newly registered workers' erroneous tentative nonconfirmation rate is no higher than permanent residents' rate measured in the same published test, on samples of each group (FY2009's 0.7% for permanent residents [EV-IMM-391] is context, not the benchmark). *If any condition fails,* the Inspector General checks again every 90 days, and the first tranche starts on the first check that passes. *Later tranches* follow one year apart. Before each, USCIS publishes the past year's erroneous nonconfirmation rates by group; if the rate for work-authorized noncitizens is above 1%, that tranche waits 90 days, and the wait repeats until the rate is at or below 1%. *No separate employer exemption or appeal process:* the tranches by size (IMM-4.12) and the error correction (IMM-4.14) are the whole of the mandate's flexibility. *On the working timeline:* filing opens about October 1, 2030; the October 2030 check fails (filing has just opened and notices are still going out), and the conditions are met by about mid-2031, so the first tranche starts about July 1, 2031 (working assumption); the later tranches about July 2032, 2033 and 2034

title: Fast error correction
parameters: (1) A tentative nonconfirmation is given to the worker in writing the same working day, in plain language and the worker's language, with how to contest it; (2) the worker has ten federal working days to contest (now eight), by phone, online or at a front door; (3) the employer may take no adverse action until the result is final, and a breach is an unfair immigration-related employment practice under 8 U.S.C. 1324b, with back pay; (4) SSA and USCIS resolve a contested case within ten federal working days, and an unresolved case closes as authorized; (5) a worker who loses work through an erroneous final nonconfirmation is paid lost wages on a short administrative claim to USCIS, with a right to sue; (6) free self-check and a lock on one's own number; (7) memo 1's statuses are loaded at registration (IMM-1.10, 1.12), so the newly legalized are confirmed automatically
agency: DHS (USCIS); SSA; DOJ (Immigrant and Employee Rights Section)

title: Employers' duties and limits
status: decided, memo 5 part 2 A; details working choices
parameters: Free: no fee for any query. Web access, a phone line and an agent route through payroll providers for small employers. No checking before a job offer and no re-checking to screen; misuse is penalized. An employer who uses E-Verify in good faith is not liable for a wrong confirmation. Civil penalties for knowingly hiring without authorization stay as in current law, with higher penalties for employers who do so to undercut wages or labor standards

title: Labor-standards enforcement
parameters: Wage and Hour and OSHA inspections targeted at the sectors with the highest violation rates (working list: agriculture, construction, care, food processing, hospitality and cleaning), and enforcement of the work routes' attestations (IMM-2.12). Funded in the agency rebuild's Wage and Hour and OSHA lines (CAP-7, legacy D9's list), already booked. The work flagship receives the items (seam)

title: Protection for workers who report abuse
parameters: A worker who files or takes part in a labor, safety, wage or discrimination complaint receives deferred action and a work permit for the complaint's duration plus six months, on the labor agency's statement of interest. Threatening a worker with immigration action, or reporting them to DHS, in retaliation is a violation with penalties. A U or T visa applicant receives a decision on bona fide status and a work permit within 180 days (working choice). Labor agencies' complaint files sit inside the firewall (IMM-1.36, 4.11)

title: Published counts for the mandate
status: working choice, from the design lens
parameters: Monthly: queries, automatic confirmations, tentative and final nonconfirmations by status group, contests and their outcomes, days to resolve, and wage claims paid (IMM-4.14). A GAO audit published before each tranche; it informs Congress and does not delay a tranche, because IMM-4.13's start check and 1% wait are the mandate's only conditions (`DEC-2026-11-12-12`)

title: Codify Trump v. Barbara in 8 U.S.C. 1401
parameters: Section 1401(a) states the Court's holding in its own words, closing the statutory route Justice Kavanaugh left open [EV-IMM-031]

title: Denaturalization limits
parameters: Only in a judicial proceeding, on clear and convincing evidence, within ten years of naturalization (except for war crimes and terrorism), and no quotas or targets

title: The test at the 2008 standard; no neighborhood investigations
parameters: The civics and English test as in 2008; USCIS's 2025 return to neighborhood investigations ends [EV-IMM-427]

title: The naturalization fee held at $760, waived below 200% of poverty, half price to 400%
parameters: N-400 at $760 [EV-IMM-422], indexed; no fee below 200% of poverty; $380 from 200% to 400%; paid for by the appropriation (IMM-6.01). DHS's June 2026 proposal [EV-IMM-423] is withdrawn

title: Naturalization ceremonies and USCIS offices as voter-registration points
status: proposed to democratic renewal, point 14; legacy DEM-1E
parameters: Each new citizen is offered registration at the ceremony

title: Public-interest work appropriated
parameters: Appropriations pay for legalization, asylum and refugee work and the naturalization discount: about $17-27 billion over FY2030-39 in all (memo 7's table), multi-year money available on enactment so USCIS hires before filing opens. It replaces the agency rebuild's USCIS line ($40 billion of CAP-7S [EV-IMM-573])

title: Fees at cost for the rest
parameters: Petitions, renewals and other benefits are fee-funded at cost, with no surcharge for waived work. The employer-paid Asylum Program Fee stays [EV-IMM-626]

title: A six-month processing target in statute
status: decided, memo 7 part 1 B; the act
parameters: Standard benefit applications decided within six months; processing times published monthly by form and office

title: Online filing for every form, front doors and the Office of New Americans
parameters: Every form online, and on paper. Statements, confirmations and corrections for the registry (IMM-1.06, 1.07) are also taken at SSA field offices, USDA Rural Development state and area offices (`DEC-2026-11-09-26`), IRS assistance centers and DOJ-recognized nonprofit legal services, which pass them to USCIS the same day. An Office of New Americans for English classes, credential recognition and integration grants

title: The pending $6 billion asylum and refugee reserve folded in
parameters: The capacity reserve's proposal [EV-IMM-578] is withdrawn; IMM-6.01's line carries the work

title: The records match: IRS, SSA and USCIS
parameters: A data agreement in statute lets USCIS ask the IRS and SSA whether records show a person's residence in given years, and receive yes or no with the years, not the returns. Each query is logged and counted. The data sits inside the firewall (IMM-1.36). A yearly fraud audit of the sworn-statement route (IMM-1.06) is published, with a review trigger: if abuse is found at scale, two documents are required per gap year The same agreement lets CMS ask USCIS whether a person holds lawful or registered status for the single plan (IMM-1.21), yes or no, inside the firewall

title: Scores requested in 2027-28
parameters: Ask CBO and JCT to score the status title and the table (IMM-1), and SSA's actuaries the Social Security effect
